faqs.q: Sec. 62-183. - Purchase and possession of graffiti materials prohibited.
faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person under the age of 18 years to purchase an aerosol
               container of paint that is capable of defacing property.
(b)
It shall be unlawful for any person to possess a masonry or glass drill bit, a carbide
               drill bit, a glass cutter, a grinding stone, an awl, a chisel, a carbide scribe, an
               aerosol paint container, a felt tip marker, or any other tool, instrument, or marking
               substance adapted, designed, or commonly used to deface property with the intent to
               commit graffiti vandalism or knowing that some person intends to use the thing possessed
               in the commission of graffiti vandalism.
(c)
It shall be unlawful for any person to carry on his person and in plain view to the
               public an aerosol container of paint while in any public facility, park, playground,
               swimming pool, beach, or recreational area, other than a highway, street, alley, or
               way, unless he has first received valid authorization from the governmental entity
               which has jurisdiction over the public area.
(d)
It shall be unlawful for any person to possess an aerosol container of paint for the
               purpose of defacing property while on any public highway, street, alley, or way, or
               other public place, regardless of whether that person is or is not in an automobile,
               vehicle, or other conveyance.
(e)
This section shall not apply to the possession of an aerosol container of paint by
               a minor for the minor's use under the supervision of the minor's parent, legal guardian,
               instructor, or employer.
(f)
Aerosol containers of paint or related substances may be furnished for use in school-related
               activities that are part of the instructional program when used under controlled and
               supervised situations within the classroom or on the site of a supervised project.
(g)
If a person under the age of 18 years is personally unable to pay a fine levied for
               acts prohibited by this article, the parent or legal guardian of that person shall
               be liable for payment of the fine.
(Code 1981, § 21-87; Ord. No. 3454, § 4, 7-6-1998)
